item.title: Community Briefs 1/29/26
item.description: County to fill over 60 board seats Lackawanna County will fill more than 60 seats on county boards, authorities or commissions that are vacant or held by members with expired terms, according to a county news release. The public is encouraged to apply. Incumbents with expired terms must submit letters of interest if they want to retain their seats. New applicants may submit a resume and a letter of interest. item.description: The Pennsylvania Association of Retired State Employees held its annual Christmas luncheon in December at Colarusso's Restaurant, Dickson City.

item.title: OPINION: Enough with the ‘CEO’ jabs at Eagles coach Nick Sirianni
item.description: The term “CEO head coach,” which is a head coach who doesn’t call plays on either side of the ball, has often been used as a backhanded slight to marginalize coaches’ accomplishments. Exhibit A: Nick Sirianni.

item.title: Carbondale Area football team, cheer squad, marching band and drill team senior members honored
item.description: This past fall, senior members of the Carbondale Area Junior/Senior High School football team, cheer squad, marching band and drill team were honored on Senior-Parent Recognition Night in their final regular season home game.

item.title: Five Questions with Mike McAndrew: Jessup to hold inaugural Groundhog Day celebration
item.description: With Groundhog Day just around the corner, most area residents have heard of Punxsutawney Phil. But how about Jessup Giuseppe? The first inaugural Jessup Groundhog Day aims to create a new borough tradition. Instead of the customary groundhog, however, this weekend's event will feature another prognosticating creature: Jessup Giuseppe, a ferret sporting a top hat.

item.title: Shining under pressure: Anthracite artist honors family with jewelry business
item.description: Jessup resident Constance Denchy descends from four generations of anthracite miners. Denchy honors this history by using anthracite in a different way: to make jewelry.

item.title: LOCAL COLLEGES: Lady Royals romp to another victory
item.description: Three players scored in double figures as the University of Scranton women’s basketball team remained unbeaten with a 76-35 win over Drew University in Landmark Conference action Wednesday at the John Long Center. Katie Gorski scored 19 points for the second-ranked Lady Royals (11-0 league, 18-0 overall). Elizabeth Bennett added 18 points and eight rebounds, while Kaci Kranson contributed 16 points. item.title: County, state legislators criticize proposed Archbald data centers
item.description: Lackawanna County Commissioner Bill Gaughan urged Archbald officials to consider the countywide impacts of data centers Wednesday night while state Rep. Kyle Mullins unequivocally opposed a proposal to build more a dozen data centers above Business Route 6.
